title: Boreal Autonomy — OEM licensing
decision_question: Should Boreal Autonomy grant North American exclusivity to an OEM for its industrial robot navigation software in 2027?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Sign a three-year exclusive OEM deal now because $2M at signing plus $300 per robot adds a large, incremental channel.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: The signing payment is a creditable advance, not extra royalty revenue; certification and direct channel overlap make unconditional exclusivity premature. A gated pilot or contingent limited exclusivity can be defensible.

key_insights.text: The $2M upfront is credited against royalties, so 2027 $1.5M of nominal royalties does not add $1.5M more cash; 2028 cash receipts are reduced by the remaining $0.5M.
2028 royalty after $80/device and $0.9M fixed OEM support yields $1.30M before the direct-channel opportunity cost.
At 65% OEM volume, 2028 standalone partner contribution is $0.53M before direct-channel tradeoffs.
Direct ARR at risk $1.8M at 82% GM represents up to $1.48M of potential incremental gross profit, not necessarily all cannibalized.
98.8% lab uptime is below 99.5% production acceptance; exclusivity effective at signature precedes necessary certification.
Nonexclusive pilot and milestone-triggered exclusivity preserve option value and contract audit rights.

required_calculations.text: Two-year nominal royalties and guarantee accounting

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Minimum guarantee credited against royalty payments
OEM support costs and possible direct channel displacement

contradictory_evidence: Bookable future devices vs paid shipped robots
Correlation of OEM exclusivity with stronger competitors growth
100% royalty margin excludes service costs and direct opportunity cost

reasoning_traps.text: Adding a recoupable advance to nominal royalties twice
Taking forecast units as audited shipments
Attributing peer growth causally to exclusivity
Ignoring support, certification and existing direct contracts

key_tradeoffs.text: Upfront liquidity vs long-term channel control
Exclusivity leverage vs direct opportunity costs
OEM upside vs certification and data risk

plausible_recommendations.text: Negotiate a nonexclusive pilot and contingent exclusivity only after certification, shipment proof and audit rights.
Accept limited geographic or time-based exclusivity with enforceable royalty minima and exit gates if incremental economics exceed channel loss.
Sign the three-year unconditional North American exclusive contract immediately based on forecast volume and gross royalty dashboard.

defensibility_criteria: No double counting of signing advance and royalties
Evaluate net support costs and potential lost direct contribution
Certification and contract audit/termination rights are binding
Compare a real nonexclusive alternative and specify decision gates

decision_requirements.question: Are the advance and credited royalties counted only once?
Does exclusivity wait for required certification?
Does partner economics include cost and channel opportunity cost?
Are enforceable partner performance exits considered?
decision_requirements.unnecessary_if: if recommending only a nonexclusive test
